# Catalytic Allene Synthesis: DOCX Formatting Fixture

## Abstract

This compact fixture exercises the academic Word export path for a chemistry review. It contains a title, abstract, keywords, section hierarchy, chemical formulae, hybridization notation, a comparison table, a numbered source list, and ordinary prose. The document is not a scientific deliverable; it is a deterministic layout and structure test used to confirm that font selection, paragraph spacing, line spacing, heading styles, scripts, tables, and references survive conversion into DOCX.

**Keywords:** allenes; catalysis; propargylic substrates; selectivity; mechanisms

## 1. Introduction

Hapticity notation such as η1-allenyl and η3-propargyl should render the numerals as real Word superscripts.

Catalytic reactions conducted under CO_2_ or H_2_O can require careful control of sp^2^ centers and S_N2_-type pathways. Unicode notation such as CO₂ and sp² should also be converted into real Word subscript and superscript runs, while locants such as C1 and publication years such as 2025 must remain ordinary text [1,2].

### 1.1 Comparison

| Method | Reagent | Main distinction |
|---|---|---|
| Palladium | $\ce{PdCl_2}$ | Carbonylative pathway |
| Nickel | CO_2_ | Electrochemical pathway |

- Preserve evidence qualifiers.
- Keep chemical notation readable.

## 2. Conclusion and Outlook

The export succeeds only when academic typography and chemical scripts are represented structurally rather than approximated with reduced-size ordinary characters [1,2].
